help.intro: Comments are written by readers on the public site - nothing here creates one. This screen is the moderation queue: what to publish, what to take down, and what to do about a thread that has gone wrong.
help.step_1_title: Know where a comment came from
help.step_1_body: A member's comment is published the moment it is written, unless the deployment turns that off; a guest's always waits here. That line is deliberate - an account can be suspended and carries a confirmed address, while a guest is a name they typed.
help.step_2_body: A comment hangs from an article or from a review, and a reply hangs from another comment. The detail window carries the guest's email and the moderation trail, which the public thread never shows; the reporter's address is only ever stored as a hash and is shown nowhere.
help.step_3_body: The status window offers only the moves allowed from where the comment is now, and nothing returns it to pending. A reason can be attached to any decision - it is kept for the audit trail, overwritten by the next decision, and never shown to the author.
help.step_4_title: Let the reports do some of the work
help.step_4_body: Three separate accounts reporting the same comment flag it on their own and take it out of the thread until someone looks. One report does not: it is as often a disagreement as a problem, and acting on it would hand every reader a mute button.
help.step_5_body: Update changes the text, the type or the pin. Changing the text marks the comment as edited in the thread - the marker is about the text no longer being what was posted, not about who rewrote it - while a pin or a type change leaves it alone. The author can rewrite their own comment too, while it is pending or approved, but not after a decision has been taken against it.
help.step_6_title: Find your way through the queue
help.step_6_body: Filter by status for the queue itself, or by target, author, type and pin. Search matches the comment text and the guest name, with no minimum length and no id shortcut - unlike every other list here.
help.note: Deleting a comment is permanent: the table has no deleted state, so there is no restore, and the whole reply subtree goes with it, along with the ratings and reports pointing at it. Reject it instead when the thread should keep its shape.
